Aggregation

Source: vignettes/aggregation.Rmd
aggregation.Rmd

aggregate_estimands() averages the treatment-group-specific estimates of multiple_treatment_group_analysis() across treatment groups, by event time (Section 5 of Leventer 2025, Identification of Child Penalties). Symbols and row labels are in Notation and output, the estimators and influence functions in Estimation. Equation, section and theorem numbers refer to the main text; appendices are referred to by name.

The examples use one simulated panel. Treatment groups 24-30 at event times 0-3 use control groups up to 34, so every treatment group has a cell at every event time.

library(childpen)
sim <- simulate_data(20000, 24:34)
res <- multiple_treatment_group_analysis(sim, 24:30, periods_post = 3,
                                         periods_pre = NULL, verbose = FALSE)

The result carries the person-level influence functions that aggregate_estimands() reads, so it is passed on unmodified.

1. Aggregate causal estimands

For event time ee, let 𝒟(e)={d:d+e<Dmax}\mathcal{D}(e) = \{d : d + e < D_{\max}\} be the treatment groups that have an estimate. Since the control group is d′=d+e+1d' = d + e + 1, the condition is d′≤Dmaxd' \le D_{\max}, the bound set by max_control_group. With 𝔼D\mathbb{E}_D the expectation over the treatment distribution, Section 5.1 defines

ρAgg(e)=𝔼D[ρ(D,D,D+e)−ρ(D,∞,D+e)∣D+e<Dmax](eq. (10)), \rho_{\mathrm{Agg}}(e) = \mathbb{E}_D\big[\rho(D, D, D + e) - \rho(D, \infty, D + e) \mid D + e < D_{\max}\big] \qquad \text{(eq. (10))}, θAgg,1(g,e)=𝔼D[θ(g,D,D+e)∣G=g,D+e<Dmax], \theta_{\mathrm{Agg},1}(g, e) = \mathbb{E}_D\big[\theta(g, D, D + e) \mid G = g,\, D + e < D_{\max}\big], θAgg,2(g,e)=𝔼D[ATE(g,D,D+e)∣G=g,D+e<Dmax]𝔼D[APO(g,D,∞,D+e)∣G=g,D+e<Dmax], \theta_{\mathrm{Agg},2}(g, e) = \frac{\mathbb{E}_D\big[\mathrm{ATE}(g, D, D + e) \mid G = g,\, D + e < D_{\max}\big]}{\mathbb{E}_D\big[\mathrm{APO}(g, D, \infty, D + e) \mid G = g,\, D + e < D_{\max}\big]}, ΔθAgg(e)=𝔼D[θ(f,D,D+e)−θ(m,D,D+e)∣D+e<Dmax](eq. (11)). \Delta\theta_{\mathrm{Agg}}(e) = \mathbb{E}_D\big[\theta(f, D, D + e) - \theta(m, D, D + e) \mid D + e < D_{\max}\big] \qquad \text{(eq. (11))}.

The package replaces each treatment-group causal estimand by its 2x2 descriptive counterpart BdB_d and the treatment distribution by weights wdw_d (next section), so that Â(e)=∑d∈𝒟(e)wdB̂d\hat A(e) = \sum_{d \in \mathcal{D}(e)} w_d \hat B_d. The rows of aggregate_estimands() are identified by method, estimand and agg_type:

method estimand agg_type aggregate BdB_d
DID_Female, DID_Male theta weighted_avg θAgg,1(g,e)\theta_{\mathrm{Agg},1}(g, e) δθ(g)\delta_\theta(g)
DID_Female, DID_Male theta ratio_of_avgs θAgg,2(g,e)\theta_{\mathrm{Agg},2}(g, e) δATE(g)\delta_{\mathrm{ATE}}(g) and δAPO(g)\delta_{\mathrm{APO}}(g), averaged separately and divided
NTD rho_effect weighted_avg ρAgg(e)\rho_{\mathrm{Agg}}(e) δΔρ\delta_{\Delta\rho}
Conventional gap_theta weighted_avg ΔθAgg(e)\Delta\theta_{\mathrm{Agg}}(e) δΔθ\delta_{\Delta\theta}
TD_E_LOGS rho_effect weighted_avg ρAgg(e)\rho_{\mathrm{Agg}}(e) under TD-E-LOGS δΔρ\delta_{\Delta\rho} with δAPO×\delta^{\times}_{\mathrm{APO}}
TD, TD_PR, accounting rows of NTD and TD_E_LOGS gap_ATE, gap_theta_pre, rho_obs, rho_cf, share_parenthood, share_other weighted_avg weighted average of the group-level row; no symbol in the paper the group-level row

The output has one row per event time, control_offset, estimand, method and agg_type, with est, se, n_groups (treatment groups with positive weight), ci_l, ci_h, t and p.

agg <- aggregate_estimands(res)
agg |>
  filter(event_time == 2, estimand %in% c("theta", "gap_theta", "rho_effect"),
         method %in% c("DID_Female", "Conventional", "NTD")) |>
  select(method, estimand, agg_type, est, se, n_groups)
#>         method   estimand      agg_type     est       se n_groups
#> 1 Conventional  gap_theta  weighted_avg -0.2273 0.004128        7
#> 2   DID_Female      theta ratio_of_avgs -0.2990 0.002595        7
#> 3   DID_Female      theta  weighted_avg -0.3033 0.002533        7
#> 4          NTD rho_effect  weighted_avg -0.2222 0.004226        7

ratio_of_avgs divides the weighted average of the ATE rows by that of the APO rows. Section 5.1 shows that θAgg,2\theta_{\mathrm{Agg},2} is also an average of the θ(g,d,d+e)\theta(g, d, d + e), with weights proportional to the treatment-group share times counterfactual earnings APO(g,d,∞,d+e)\mathrm{APO}(g, d, \infty, d + e).

2. Weights

weights weight of treatment group dd in 𝒟(e)\mathcal{D}(e)
"sample" (default) the share of persons in the group: wd=nd/∑k∈𝒟(e)nkw_d = n_d / \sum_{k \in \mathcal{D}(e)} n_k, where ndn_d counts persons of both genders with D=dD = d. For DID_Female and DID_Male, shares within gender: wg,d=ng,d/∑k∈𝒟(e)ng,kw_{g,d} = n_{g,d} / \sum_{k \in \mathcal{D}(e)} n_{g,k}
"uniform" or NULL 1/me1/m_e, with mem_e the number of groups in 𝒟(e)\mathcal{D}(e)
a named numeric vector proportional to the entry named dd, renormalized to sum to one over 𝒟(e)\mathcal{D}(e). Groups missing from the vector get weight zero, with a warning

Gender gaps are aggregated as in eq. (11): the within-group gap is averaged with weights pooled over genders, rather than differencing two within-gender aggregates, which would also reflect gender differences in the treatment distribution (Section 5.1). Only DID_Female and DID_Male use within-gender weights.

w_named <- setNames(dnorm(24:30, mean = 27, sd = 3), 24:30)
bind_rows(
  sample  = aggregate_estimands(res, weights = "sample",  methods = "NTD"),
  uniform = aggregate_estimands(res, weights = "uniform", methods = "NTD"),
  named   = aggregate_estimands(res, weights = w_named,   methods = "NTD"),
  .id = "weights"
) |>
  filter(estimand == "rho_effect", event_time %in% c(0, 3)) |>
  select(weights, event_time, est, se, n_groups)
#>   weights event_time     est       se n_groups
#> 1  sample          0 -0.2767 0.005244        7
#> 2  sample          3 -0.1970 0.004096        7
#> 3 uniform          0 -0.2843 0.005427        7
#> 4 uniform          3 -0.2044 0.004060        7
#> 5   named          0 -0.2840 0.005471        7
#> 6   named          3 -0.2045 0.004017        7

A named vector aggregates the same treatment-group estimates under another treatment distribution, as in Figure 9 of the paper (Replicating the paper).

Groups that drop out. A treatment group has a cell at event time ee only if its control group d+e+1d + e + 1 is at most max_control_group (DmaxD_{\max} in the paper). Groups beyond the bound drop out at later event times, and n_groups records how many remain.

res_cap <- multiple_treatment_group_analysis(sim, 24:30, periods_post = 3, periods_pre = NULL,
                                             max_control_group = 32, verbose = FALSE)
bind_rows(
  `Inf` = aggregate_estimands(res,     methods = "NTD"),
  `32`  = aggregate_estimands(res_cap, methods = "NTD"),
  .id = "max_control_group"
) |>
  filter(estimand == "rho_effect") |>
  select(max_control_group, event_time, est, n_groups)
#>   max_control_group event_time     est n_groups
#> 1               Inf          0 -0.2767        7
#> 2               Inf          1 -0.2516        7
#> 3               Inf          2 -0.2222        7
#> 4               Inf          3 -0.1970        7
#> 5                32          0 -0.2767        7
#> 6                32          1 -0.2516        7
#> 7                32          2 -0.2360        6
#> 8                32          3 -0.2148        5

With max_control_group = 32, group 30 has cells at e=0,1e = 0, 1 only and group 29 at e≤2e \le 2, so 𝒟(e)\mathcal{D}(e) shrinks and the weights change with ee. As the footnote to eq. (10) notes (following Callaway and Sant’Anna 2021), a comparison of aggregates across ee then combines variation in causal effects with a shift in the composition of treatment groups. The composition is the same at every event time when each group in the aggregate has a cell at each of them, as with max_control_group = Inf above (n_groups is 7 throughout).

3. Standard errors

Let BdB_d be the estimate of treatment group dd, pd=Pr⁡(D=d)p_d = \Pr(D = d) its population share, Pe=∑d∈𝒟(e)pdP_e = \sum_{d \in \mathcal{D}(e)} p_d and wd=pd/Pew_d = p_d / P_e. The influence function of A(e)=∑d∈𝒟(e)wdBdA(e) = \sum_{d \in \mathcal{D}(e)} w_d B_d is (the aggregate estimator section of the appendix on estimation and inference) ψA(e)=1Pe∑d∈𝒟(e)[(Bd−A(e))ψpd+pdψBd],ψpd=1{D=d}−pd. \psi_{A(e)} = \frac{1}{P_e} \sum_{d \in \mathcal{D}(e)} \Big[ \big(B_d - A(e)\big)\,\psi_{p_d} + p_d\,\psi_{B_d} \Big], \qquad \psi_{p_d} = 1\{D = d\} - p_d . For the within-gender rows the share is the joint share of gender gg and group dd, with 1{G=g,D=d}−pg,d1\{G = g, D = d\} - p_{g,d} in place of ψpd\psi_{p_d}. With "uniform" or fixed weights the first term is absent; with "sample" it accounts for the estimated shares. For ratio_of_avgs, θ̂Agg,2=N̂/M̂\hat\theta_{\mathrm{Agg},2} = \hat N / \hat M with N̂=∑dwdδ̂ATE,d\hat N = \sum_d w_d\,\hat\delta_{\mathrm{ATE},d} and M̂=∑dwdδ̂APO,d\hat M = \sum_d w_d\,\hat\delta_{\mathrm{APO},d}, and by the chain rule (not in the paper) ψθAgg,2=ψNM−NψMM2, \psi_{\theta_{\mathrm{Agg},2}} = \frac{\psi_N}{M} - \frac{N\,\psi_M}{M^2}, where ψN\psi_N and ψM\psi_M are the influence functions of the two weighted averages, each with its share term. The influence function of share_other is minus that of share_parenthood.

The group-level influence functions are summed per person across treatment groups before they are squared, with clusters at the person level, Var̂(Â)=1n2∑c(∑i∈cψ̂i)2GG−1, \widehat{\mathrm{Var}}(\hat A) = \frac{1}{n^2} \sum_{c} \Big( \sum_{i \in c} \hat\psi_i \Big)^2 \frac{G}{G - 1}, for nn person-age rows and GG persons. A person who serves as a control group member for several treatment groups therefore enters several terms of the same sum. The share term is put on the person-age scale with the average number of ages per person, which is exact for a balanced panel. The estimators and the influence functions of the group-level rows are in Estimation.
